correctness.rationale: The generator and time normalization are checked against the projective Brownian source. Applying the explicit positive Green operator K to 1 gives the known mean. Fubini gives J(1)=H_{n-1}/(n-1)^2; monotonicity of the weighted average J/W proves 0<Km<alpha*m and its sharp endpoint ratio. A positive convergent resolvent series and bounded optional stopping establish the Laplace transform, finite-threshold bound and its asymptotically exact coefficient. Differentiation at s=0 yields the strict CV deficit. A separate 186-check high-precision script compares hypergeometric ODE derivatives, quadrature, bounds, and finite-threshold examples. No finite experiment is used to prove an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The 2026 projective Brownian model motivates the time required to attain nearly perfect quantum-state fidelity. A mere long-time exponential tail does not quantify the entire normalized waiting-time law, while the sharp first-order finite-fidelity coefficient and strict variability deficit quantify the reliability of high-fidelity geometric state exploration across Hilbert dimensions. The explicit harmonic coefficient and finite-parameter bound are nontrivial quantitative results, not a restatement of a numerical table or textbook exercise.
